articles.title: Join Us: Watch 11 Minutes of Exclusive Gameplay from the Upcoming Cult Simulator | gamescom 2026
articles.summary: Join Us, the upcoming open-world co-op game where you can start your very own doomsday cult, just dropped a ton of new gameplay as part of IGN's gamescom programming. You can see more than 11 minutes of exclusive footage in the player below, and get a deeper look into just how the game will work.
body: Earlier this week, developer Wolf Haus games announced that the darkly satirical survival/action cult simulator will be available on PS5 at launch alongside the PC and Xbox Series X/S versions in March 2027. The news of Join Us' PS5 version also featured information on how 4-player co-op will work in both the campaign and free roam.

The live-action trailer featuring former cult members, which you can watch below, introduces us to Jaga, Javier, Ariel, and Elena - who have a "collective experience of over 50 years in their unique societies." This experience involves a cult that is preparing for aliens to arrive on Earth and take us back to the planet we came from, a peaceful cult that focuses on martial arts and self-defense training, and a holistic rejuvenation cult.

In Join Us, players will need to stay vigilant though, as they'll need to keep their recruits happy or they will leave the cult. As the devs put it, "a cult leader without any followers is just a lonely weirdo."
For more from gamescom, be sure to check out everything that was revealed during Opening Night Live.

articles.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Will Send You On a Chilly Loot Grind | gamescom 2026
articles.summary: Dragon's Dogma 2's Dark Arisen expansion adds a whole new region with clever winter weather effects, an old-but-new loot grind, and... a dragon that vomits zombies. We're so back.
body: There are plenty of fantastical creatures to fight in Dragon’s Dogma 2, but nowhere in the base game will you find a dragon that vomits zombies. You will find such a beast in its upcoming Dark Arisen expansion, though, and this winged atrocity marked the final challenge of a 90-minute hands-on demo I played just ahead of gamescom 2026.

The undead barfer easily ranks among Dragon’s Dogma 2’s most hideous foes – a scaly titan with an unsightly face, torn wings, and decaying flesh. At multiple points throughout the battle, it rears back its head to belch a plume of sinister smoke from its rotting maw, out of which skitters a gang of pallid corpses. It’s a creative and horrific way to introduce additional mobs to a boss fight, and for a moment I’m distracted from my project of hacking the dragon’s legs off to perform a series of spinning sword attacks, cutting down the newly-birthed fodder three at a time.
points: Dragon's Dogma 2's Dark Arisen expansion adds a whole new region with clever winter weather effects, an old-but-new loot grind, and... a dragon that vomits zombies.

articles.title: Alan Ritchson's New 103-Minute Action Revenge Thriller Is an Instant Streaming Hit
articles.summary: Action star Alan Ritchson has been a dominant force on streaming thanks to his Prime Video series Reacher and Netflix's sci-fi action hit War Machine. Ritchson's latest film, Motor City, debuted in movie theaters in July, but the one-man-army revenge thriller didn't knock out audiences.
body: Motor City was released digitally on Aug. 26. Within days of its release, Motor City has already landed in the top 10 purchases on Prime Video (where it's currently No. 9) and on Apple TV (where it's No. 4), further proving that when it comes to Alan Ritchson delivering brutal beat-downs, action movie fans prefer to watch them in the comfort of their own home.

Ritchson has carved out a niche as Hollywood's most lovable big guy, a brand he continues in Motor City. Ritchson plays John Miller, a "working-class romantic" who's framed by a ruthless gangster after falling for the wrong woman. After spending years in prison, Miller returns with only one mission: revenge. In Motor City, action — not talk — is the name of the game. According to one of the film's stars, Motor City only has "five lines of dialogue."
In 1970s Detroit, John Miller falls for a local gangster's girl and lands in prison for a crime he didn't commit. Life ruined, Miller plots revenge against the man who took his girl away.
The following action clip offers a taste of what Motor City has to offer: guns, violence, and a driving rock 'n' roll score.

articles.title: Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch'd & Pichu gets first trailer
articles.summary: The Pokémon Company International and Aardman have released the first teaser trailer for Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch'd & Pichu, a new stop-motion series set in the Galar region.
body: The video description teases: "Join our unlikely heroes, Sirfetch'd and Pichu, in their gallant quest to protect Pokémon across Galar! While their missions might rarely go as planned, their noble deeds forge their friendship as they step bravely into the unknown. Peril, alliances, rivalries, extraordinary Pokémon, and endless laughs await them."

Pokémon's director of original animation Phil Rynda joined Aardman's Tom Parkinson (director), Nat McKay (creative director, IP development), and James Young (model-making creative lead) on the panel to walk fans through the show's puppets, sets, and production process.
Disney+ was also confirmed as the series' exclusive worldwide streaming home when it arrives in 2027, following the platform's recent addition of Pokémon the Series: The Beginning.

Set across the wilds of Galar, Pokémon Tales follows Sirfetch'd and Pichu on what Pokémon describes as "a gallant quest to help and protect Pokémon across the region", with new Pokémon and location reveals including Obstagoon and the Crown Tundra area, both previously seen in Pokémon Sword and Shield.

articles.title: Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is aiming to be the "definitive" game for the setting, and I think it might be exactly that
articles.summary: In a small room inside a crowded Koelnesse convention centre, a short presentation on Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is shown to a gaggle of tired writers. Creative Assembly's brand manager says they're hoping to make the definitive game in the 40k universe.
body: The game is, like all Total War games, a grand strategy, set in an especially chaotic corner of a war-torn galaxy. In the demo I played, I was able to experience a slice of the tutorial campaign and the main campaign, plus a challenging large-scale battle to wrap up. It was a small window into what is looking to be a gargantuan tactical experience: nonetheless I left convinced of its merit.

First off, the presentation here is brilliant. Everything looks just right, sounds just right. A bolter erupts with just the right force, and looks exactly as it should. A dreadnought, stomping across the map, does so with the weight it deserves. There's this thing I do in Total War sometimes: I zoom right up close to fights to get right into the action. Doing so here is like opening a portal into the grim darkness of Warhammer 40,000. This game is Creative Assembly's first 18 rated game and it shows: Orks running into your firing line erupt in a carnival of gore.

articles.title: Rachel McAdams' 10/10 Time-Travel Movie Is Officially Coming to Streaming Next Week
articles.summary: Nobody in the history of cinema has had more time-traveling husbands than Rachel McAdams. Four years after she starred in The Time Traveler’s Wife (2009) opposite Eric Bana, McAdams played Mary in About Time (2013).
body: Written and directed by Richard Curtis ( Love Actually, Notting Hill ), About Time is structured around Domhnall Gleeson’s voiceover, not as a guide through the plot, but as something closer to a private journal. Tim doesn’t narrate like someone who knows how his story ends. He narrates like someone revisiting moments he didn’t fully understand at the time.

Gleeson’s delivery is key. His voice is warm, slightly hesitant, and unshowy, which makes the film’s big ideas feel intimate. When he talks about his family — especially his sister “Kit Kat” — there’s affection in the humorous ways he describes their quirks.

Even when the movie introduces its time-travel conceit, it does so casually. Tim’s father, played by Bill Nighy hamming it up with lots of charm, tells his son about their shared ability (which only the men of the family possess) without ever making it feel like a superpower. Instead, it’s a tool for introspection and being mindfully present in life. That philosophy becomes the focus of the entire story and the reason About Time ultimately has more to say about living in the present than it does about changing the past.

articles.title: The Dog Stars Release Date Window for Disney Plus Streaming, Blu-ray, and DVD
articles.summary: Ridley Scott’s latest sci-fi film, The Dog Stars, has divided critics. While Polygon loved the moody tale of a pilot (Jacob Elordi) searching for meaning in a world where most of humanity was wiped out by a deadly flu, other publications were less enthusiastic about the slow pace and wild tone…
body: Here’s what we know about when The Dog Stars will be available digitally and on DVD.

We expect that The Dog Stars will follow the pattern of other 20th Century Studios films. Avatar: Fire and Ash premiered in theaters on Dec. 19, 2025, and got its digital release on March 31, while Predator: Badlands made its VOD debut on Jan. 6 after opening on Nov. 7, 2025. The Dog Stars premiered on Aug. 28, so that means it will probably land on VOD by the end of October.

20th Century Studios tends to wait about six weeks between digital and physical releases. Avatar: Fire and Ash got its physical release on May 19, while Predator: Badlands came out on 4K UHD, DVD, and Blu-ray on Feb. 17. That means you’ll probably see a special feature-packed The Dog Stars physical release in December.

articles.title: What we've been playing - "Forget the classics: remaster the duds"
articles.summary: Hello and welcome back to our regular feature where we write a little about the games we've been playing. This week, Kelsey didn't have to sacrifice a limb to play Elden Ring for the first time again; Bertie mucks around in the Prancing Pony with edgy Aragorn; and the rest of the team travels back…
body: Here's another question: do you remember what you were playing last week? You don't have to! The What We've Been Playing archive has you covered.

I've already written at length about the opening hours of my experience with Elden Ring on the Nintendo Switch 2, and spoilers in case you've not read it yet, but it's not half-bad. There's a few frame drops here and there and I worry how, later, the faster, more-demanding bosses will fare. But so far it's honestly just really nice to be able to alternate between playing the game docked and handheld.

Sure, I find the text a little small on handheld, but the sheer novelty of being able to play Elden Ring wherever I am is something I've been longing for for years (without having to buy a Steam Deck, that is). It's also been lovely to experience the game from the very beginning again after years of barrelling through New Game Plus and randomisers galore. I always joke about how I'd sacrifice a limb to play Elden Ring for the first time again (I wouldn't really, but still), and playing it from fresh on the Switch 2 has certainly come pretty close to that being a reality (and my limbs are still intact!).

articles.title: Marvel Star's Forgotten 100-Minute Action Thriller Is About to Disappear From Streaming
articles.summary: There's a particular sort of movie that's fallen out of style in the 2020s, as the film industry has pivoted to a sort of feast-or-famine style for theatrical distribution. Currently, anything that gets a run on the big screen is either a blockbuster with a nine-digit budget or an indie production.
body: Movie theaters used to have a well-established middle ground, which was the traditional domain of comedies, higher-concept thrillers, and occasionally action movies. These weren't meant to be the [genre] event of the summer, Oscar bait, or a billion-dollar cultural event. Instead, they were workhorse midcarders, here to entertain you for an evening, then go on to a respectable existence as something you'd catch on cable or an airplane now and again.

Legion, a Biblically-themed zombie-ish action/horror movie starring Paul Bettany as a heavily-armed archangel, is a perfect example. With Bettany's star on the rise following the announcement of the forthcoming VisionQuest series on Disney Plus, now's a good time to dip back into the weirder side of his filmography, but you'll have to act fast. 2010's Legion is leaving Netflix on Aug. 31.

Legion, not to be confused with the 2017 TV show, begins with the archangel Michael (Bettany) falling to Earth in downtown Los Angeles. He cuts off his own wings, raids a local warehouse for all the guns he can carry, then steals a police car. As one does.

articles.title: The Pokémon Company Looks to Smart Device Integrations as Future Targets
articles.summary: President and CEO of The Pokémon Company, Tsunekazu Ishihara, shared a small bit of insight about the company’s possible future plans with wearable technology during a panel discussion at the inaugural PokémonXP in San Francisco, CA. During the Producing Pokémon: A Conversation with Mr.
body: “In the past, these gadgets or companion accessories [like the Pokéwalker and PokémonGO Plus] were kind of like these cool secret weapons you could pull out of your pocket and do something really cool with,” Ishihara said, “ but today I was thinking, going forward, maybe a challenge for us is going to be figuring out how we can integrate Pokémon more with some of the wearable technology, like smart watches, smart glasses, or even smart rings, for example.” The comment comes on the tail of the reveal of the Fitbit Air Special Edition Pokémon Sleep, a wearable health tracker with full connectivity to Pokémon Sleep, a Pokémon app that essentially gamifies sleep into collecting Pokémon.

Ishihara is also the founder and previous CEO of Creatures Inc., a co-owner of the Pokémon franchise alongside Nintendo and Game Freak, who together make The Pokémon Company International. Ishihara has experienced the complete history of the franchise, from Pokémon Red and Pokémon Green to the conception of the anime and trading card game. During the panel, Ishihara said he’s always loved handheld gadgets and toys and is particularly passionate about them.

articles.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil on Track to Have Biggest Opening Weekend of Any RE Movie in History
articles.summary: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie is on track to have the most profitable opening weekend out of any film adaptation of Capcom’s flagship horror franchise. Stats aggregated by Box Office Pro, a business-to-business trade magazine and the official publication of the National Association of Theater…
body: The zombie flick is projected to earn $40M – $50M during its opening weekend this September — an amount that would make it the most financially successful opening weekend for any Resident Evil movie ever released in theaters.
For comparison, the highest amount earned during an opening weekend for a Resident Evil movie was for Resident Evil: Afterlife, which netted $26,650,26 when it opened in 2010.

Enthusiasm for Cregger’s take on the series is at an all-time high, even though the famous filmmaker has publicly eschewed the idea of creating a 1:1 adaptation of the games. Rather than trying to live up to what fans have already played, Cregger follows an average Joe who gets caught up in the Racoon City Incident — and so far, it’s looking pretty solid.

Cregger has included more than a few cheeky references to the games (the main character scrambling for ammo, Heavy Field shotgun shells from Resident Evil 4, first-person action sequences, a typewriter and the mention of Umbrella), and considering his impressive resume of highly-lauded horror films ( Barbarian, Weapons ), this fresh take on the beloved video game franchise experiencing a good about of hype.

articles.title: Hello Neighbor's multiplayer spinoff has been 'temporarily shut down' after a hacker wiped player progression and demanded the game's 'removal from sale across all platforms'
articles.summary: Secret Neighbor, the multiplayer spinoff for the 2017 horror game Hello Neighbor, has been temporarily taken offline following a security breach by a hacker who accessed the game's backend systems and deleted player data.
body: The incident, which occurred last week, involved an individual who obtained credentials with admin access to the game. The hacker then proceeded to wipe player profiles, in-game progression, and other data, while also carrying out what developer Hologryph and publisher tinyBuild described as a "coordinated attack on our server systems and infrastructure" across all platforms.

Hologryph and tinyBuild addressed the situation in a Steam post, (via delistedgames ). They explained that, in addition to the attack, the hacker had "stated they intend to continue targeting the game and its backend systems until the game is removed from sale across all platforms."

According to both companies, no personal data or information had been compromised by the attack. Yet as the incident is ongoing, they have opted to "temporarily shut down the game until we had addressed the breach and closed any vulnerabilities that may have led to the incident."

In its statement, Hologryph and tinyBuild say they have alerted the relevant authorities to the situation. They are also working with PlayFab—the company which provides Secret Neighbour's backend services—in an attempt to recover the data that has been wiped.

articles.title: Tech Experts Call Grand Theft Auto 6 The Most Visually Advanced Game To Date, Which Explains Why It’s Stuck At 30FPS
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally had its first big gameplay reveal, giving us our first real look at Rockstar's massive open-world and the amount of detail it holds. It's one that might be the most visually-impressive game we've ever seen, according to the experts at Digital Foundry.
body: Digital Foundry's Oliver Mackenzie and Richard Leadbetter have praised GTA 6's visual presentation, with Mackenzie specifically going as far to call it the "most impressive example of real-time game rendering" he's ever seen. The pair praised a slew of details showcased in the gameplay, including standout character rendering, especially the hair physics and skin details across not just the game's protagonist, but many NPCs too.

Ray tracing use was also praised, with the pair pointing out how Rockstar has delicately implemented it in the right places for the biggest impact, and is leaning on older conventional methods in the pursuit for a better balance between fidelity and performance.

Performance was a big talking point too, especially so given how poorly GTA 5 performed on Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 when it initially launched. Rockstar has always seemingly favored the best looking image quality over the smoothest, but that seems to have changed with GTA 6. Digital Foundry noted that while the game was rendering at 30 frames per second, that target seems to be consistently hit, with the team rarely finding dips during its analysis of all 48,242 frames.

videos.title: Here's How GTA 6's Map Compares to GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 - IGN Daily Fix
videos.summary: Rockstar finally dropped their extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and the game looks as dense as any GTA game before it. In fact, according to Rockstar, the map for GTA 6 is twice the size of GTA 5's, and three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2.
body: Presented by Universal Orlando Resort, and its newest theme park, Universal Epic Universe.
points: Rockstar finally dropped their extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and the game looks as dense as any GTA game before it.
In fact, according to Rockstar, the map for GTA 6 is twice the size of GTA 5's, and three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2.
Rockstar North's co-studio head Rob Nelson also revealed that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game while primarily focusing on story missions.
In other news, eagle-eyed fans spotted a Red Dead 2 easter egg in the new GTA 6 footage.
